papers.title: RESILAGENT: A Three-Pillar Architecture for Cyber-Physical Resilience in Electrical Power and Energy Systems
papers.abstract_en: Electrical Power and Energy Systems face hybrid threats that combine cyber intrusions, physical sabotage and climate-driven stress, and routinely outpace today's siloed monitoring stacks. We present RESILAGENT, a concept architecture organised around three operational pillars, Sensing & Data Intelligence, Resilience Analytics & Reporting, and Incident Response & Recovery, mediated by a Cloud-based Orchestrator and exercised through a closed Detect-Simulate-Decide-Sign loop. The framework fuses agentic artificial intelligence and multimodal large language models for cross-modal detection, real-time digital twins for what-if simulation, and a permissioned blockchain anchor for tamper-evident threat intelligence and CER/NIS2-aligned evidence. We instantiate it on two scenarios, a transmission operator under coordinated cyber compromise, sabotage and heatwave, and a distribution operator under a supply-chain compromise during a storm, and report an IEEE-bus micro-benchmark that quantifies each pillar through false-data-injection attack detection, cyber-physical fusion lift, N-1 contingency screening and anchor cost.

summary_es.tldr: RESILAGENT protege redes eléctricas contra amenazas híbridas combinando IA, gemelos digitales y blockchain para una resiliencia sin precedentes.
summary_es.problema: Los sistemas eléctricos enfrentan amenazas híbridas (ciberataques, sabotaje, estrés climático) que superan las soluciones de monitoreo actuales y aisladas.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone RESILAGENT, una arquitectura de tres pilares (Detección Inteligente, Análisis de Resiliencia, Respuesta a Incidentes) orquestada en la nube, utilizando IA, LLMs multimodales, gemelos digitales y blockchain para un ciclo de detección, simulación y recuperación.
summary_es.resultados: La arquitectura se probó en dos escenarios y un micro-benchmark que cuantificó la detección de ataques de inyección de datos falsos, la mejora en la fusión ciber-física y el costo de la cadena de bloques.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Proporciona un marco unificado y robusto para mejorar la resiliencia de las infraestructuras críticas de energía, crucial para la estabilidad social y económica.

papers.title: STA: A Split Temporal Adversary Method for Evaluating Robustness of Multimodal RL-based Driving Policies
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal reinforcement learning (MRL) offers a promising paradigm for autonomous driving by jointly leveraging complementary sensor observations to learn effective decision-making policies. However, its effectiveness critically depends on temporal alignment across modalities, making temporal inconsistency a fundamental vulnerability. Even subtle misalignment or latency can corrupt fused representations and ultimately lead to decision failures. Existing studies have explored adversarial attacks to induce cross-modal temporal inconsistencies, thereby enabling systematic evaluation of the temporal robustness of MRL policies. However, existing methods remain limited in generality, realism, and adaptivity. To address these limitations, we propose the Split Temporal Adversary (STA), which formulates multimodal temporal attacks as a unified decision process that jointly optimizes attack timing and modality selection under realistic policy-aware and budget-constrained settings. STA includes two mechanisms: a) a unified multimodal temporal perturbation mechanism that delays observations via historical states, removing the need for modality-specific noise; b) a split multimodal adversarial decision mechanism that jointly optimizes attack timing and modality selection through adaptive optimization while leveraging the victim policy's clean actions to identify sensitive decision patterns. We provide a theoretical analysis of the induced distribution shift and a modality selection principle. Experiments in the CARLA simulator show that STA more than doubles the collision rate of the strongest baseline against PPO while using 17.8\% fewer attack attempts, and that it generalizes to a VLM-based driving policy. These results reveal temporal consistency as a critical vulnerability, highlighting temporal robustness as essential for safe autonomous driving.

summary_es.tldr: Atacante temporal dividido (STA) evalúa la robustez de la conducción autónoma multimodal, superando a los métodos actuales.
summary_es.problema: Las políticas de conducción autónoma multimodal son vulnerables a la desalineación temporal entre sensores, lo que puede causar fallos en la toma de decisiones.
summary_es.propuesta: STA, un método de ataque temporal dividido, optimiza conjuntamente el momento del ataque y la selección de modalidad, introduciendo perturbaciones temporales unificadas y adaptándose a la política víctima.
summary_es.resultados: STA duplica la tasa de colisión contra PPO con menos intentos de ataque (17.8% menos) y se generaliza a políticas basadas en VLM, demostrando su eficacia.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Garantizar la robustez temporal es crucial para la seguridad de la conducción autónoma, y STA proporciona una forma más realista y efectiva de evaluar esta vulnerabilidad.

papers.title: ProcReverser: Multi-Agent Black-Box Microarchitectural Reverse Engineering for Processor Vulnerability Analysis
papers.abstract_en: When processor implementation details are unavailable, black-box microarchitectural reverse engineering helps security researchers identify hardware conditions related to security vulnerabilities. However, this process requires substantial manual effort to design experiments, develop test programs, and analyze results for each processor. We present ProcReverser, a multi-agent system that automates this process. ProcReverser uses execution feedback to improve experimental plans and test programs and identifies microarchitectural properties from measurements. We develop a comprehensive suite of property identification tasks focused on hardware mechanisms relevant to Spectre-class attacks, covering speculative execution, branch prediction, memory dependence, and cache behavior. We evaluate ProcReverser on the XuanTie C910, the gem5 RISC-V O3 CPU model, and the SiFive P550. ProcReverser achieves Pass@1 and Pass@5 scores of 81.3% and 93.8%, respectively, on C910, and 83.0% and 100.0% on gem5 O3. On the SiFive P550, ProcReverser further characterizes microarchitectural properties covered by the proposed task suite. These findings highlight the potential of automated microarchitectural reverse engineering to support processor vulnerability analysis and defense evaluation.

summary_es.tldr: ProcReverser automatiza la ingeniería inversa de microarquitecturas de procesadores para encontrar vulnerabilidades de seguridad.
summary_es.problema: Identificar detalles de microarquitectura de procesadores para analizar vulnerabilidades de seguridad es un proceso manual, lento y costoso que requiere mucho esfuerzo.
summary_es.propuesta: ProcReverser es un sistema multiagente que automatiza el diseño de experimentos, la creación de programas de prueba y el análisis de resultados para inferir propiedades microarquitectónicas relevantes para ataques como Spectre.
summary_es.resultados: ProcReverser alcanzó puntuaciones Pass@1 del 81.3% y Pass@5 del 93.8% en el procesador XuanTie C910, y del 83.0% y 100.0% en el modelo gem5 O3. También caracterizó propiedades en el SiFive P550.
summary_es.por_que_importa: La automatización de este proceso acelera significativamente el análisis de vulnerabilidades en procesadores, permitiendo un desarrollo de defensas más rápido y eficaz.

papers.title: Severe but Harmless: Stress-Testing Shift Severity for Frozen Time-Series Forecasters
papers.abstract_en: Zero-shot time-series foundation models (TSFMs) have become attractive alternatives to task-specific models because they handle diverse downstream tasks, including anomaly detection and forecasting, without per-series training. However, time-series data undergo distribution shifts, and the dissimilarity between two regimes is commonly scored with statistical measures such as Wasserstein-1, where a higher score is read as a more severe shift. In systematic experiments using three established severity measures on nine regime shifts from three standard traffic datasets, we show that these measures do not reliably predict degradation for instance-normalized TSFMs. The regimes rated most severe are not the regimes that degrade the models most, and degradation reaches 29% in the lowest-scoring regime. In most cases, the audit shows no positive relationship between measured severity and model degradation. We provide an equivariance-based stress-testing analysis that explains why severity readings can become decoupled from model degradation.

summary_es.tldr: Las métricas actuales de "severidad" de cambios en datos de series temporales no predicen la degradación de modelos de IA, incluso empeorando el rendimiento.
summary_es.problema: Los modelos de IA para series temporales (TSFM) fallan ante cambios en los datos (distribution shifts), pero las métricas actuales para medir la "severidad" de estos cambios no predicen de forma fiable cuánto se degradará el modelo.
summary_es.propuesta: Se realiza un análisis de "stress-testing" basado en la equivariancia para explicar por qué las métricas de severidad no se correlacionan con la degradación real del modelo en TSFMs normalizados.
summary_es.resultados: Se demostró que las métricas de severidad comunes no predicen la degradación del modelo. En algunos casos, la degradación alcanzó el 29% en los regímenes calificados como menos severos, y en la mayoría de los casos no hubo relación positiva entre la severidad medida y la degradación del modelo.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Es crucial para evaluar la robustez de los modelos de IA en el mundo real, donde los datos cambian constantemente. Las métricas actuales pueden ser engañosas, llevando a una falsa sensación de seguridad o a subestimar problemas críticos.

papers.title: Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. Current fixes, such as checklists, reviewer models and LLM judges, ask the model to catch it. But models often see the problem and answer anyway. We present SilentGuard, which moves the decision from the model to the harness running tool calls. It tests each result against invariants that any correct API must satisfy and withholds values that break one. We find silent failures in 11 of 15 public research APIs, with counts inflated up to 691 times. Current fixes leave over 70% of answers wrong, and agents report 77.4% of counts a judge flags. Across 7 open models, SilentGuard cuts wrong answers on its target faults from 74.0% to 1.7%, with no loss on fault-free tasks. On three frontier models they fall from 70.2% to 0.5%. A warning from the same check leaves 70.1% wrong, so enforcement is the key. On new fault types, the harness alone cuts wrong answers from 61.1% to 24.5%. It avoids wrong answers by abstaining rather than recovering.

summary_es.tldr: Protege a los agentes de IA de fallos silenciosos de API que devuelven datos incorrectos pero válidos.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes de IA que usan APIs pueden recibir respuestas erróneas (fallos silenciosos) que parecen correctas (HTTP 200) pero contienen información incorrecta, lo que lleva a decisiones equivocadas. Las soluciones actuales, como revisiones por modelos, no son efectivas.
summary_es.propuesta: SilentGuard, un sistema que se integra en el 'harness' (la capa que ejecuta las llamadas a la API) para verificar los resultados de las APIs contra 'invariantes' predefinidas. Si un resultado viola estas reglas, se considera un fallo y no se entrega al agente.
summary_es.resultados: SilentGuard redujo las respuestas incorrectas debidas a fallos silenciosos del 74.0% al 1.7% en modelos abiertos y del 70.2% al 0.5% en modelos de vanguardia. Detectó fallos silenciosos en 11 de 15 APIs públicas, con aumentos de hasta 691 veces en recuentos. Las soluciones actuales dejan más del 70% de las respuestas incorrectas.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Asegura la fiabilidad de los agentes de IA en entornos reales al prevenir que tomen decisiones basadas en datos de API erróneos pero aparentemente válidos, mejorando drásticamente su precisión y seguridad.

papers.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
reasons: 🎯 temas: AI agents, fintech & payments, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Tool-using agents act on email, files, and payments, so an instruction hidden in a web page or a shared document can make an agent send data or money to an attacker. Many runtime defenses put a language model on the decision that lets an action through, so the decision depends on a model that may read the attacker's text and adds model calls to every step. Provenance defenses keep the model off the final check but need a model to plan or route each task first. Where an action goes can instead be read from the tools' typed returns: an email's sender or a payment's account arrives in a typed field, while injected instructions arrive as free text. SPILLWAY turns this observation into a deterministic floor with no per-task plan. The check admits a call when each target value that appears in tool output but not in the user's task was returned by a read-only tool in a typed field or is covered by a fixed delegation rule. A deterministic sanitizer removes instruction-like regions its fixed rules match before the model reads them and retains the removed spans as evidence, and a local judge may restore a refused call, never one whose target lies in the removed text. Across three backbones, and seven task suites on one of them, no standard templated injection redirects an action to an attacker's target under SPILLWAY, at the highest observed mean utility and composite scores (NRP, ERS) of the defenses we run under that attack. A forged chat template also produces a raw zero, and mean in-scope attack success under a released reinforcement-learning attacker is .005. SPILLWAY reaches this floor with no defense-triggered backbone re-run and almost no added model call. As personal AI agents act on users' email, files, and payments, SPILLWAY gives them an auditable refusal floor on where their actions go that keeps them useful and holds across backbones.

summary_es.tldr: SPILLWAY defiende agentes de IA contra inyecciones maliciosas separando la admisión de objetivos de la sanitización, garantizando seguridad y utilidad.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes de IA que usan herramientas (para email, pagos, etc.) son vulnerables a ataques de inyección de prompts, donde instrucciones ocultas pueden redirigir acciones o datos a atacantes, comprometiendo la seguridad.
summary_es.propuesta: SPILLWAY propone separar la admisión de objetivos de la sanitización. Utiliza las salidas tipadas de las herramientas para verificar los objetivos de las acciones, distinguiendo entre datos legítimos y texto libre inyectado. Implementa un sanitizador determinista que elimina regiones de instrucciones antes de que el modelo las lea y un juez local para restaurar llamadas rechazadas.
summary_es.resultados: SPILLWAY bloquea inyecciones de prompts estándar, logrando las puntuaciones más altas en utilidad y métricas compuestas (NRP, ERS) frente a otros métodos. Un ataque de plantilla de chat forjada resulta en cero éxito, y un atacante de aprendizaje por refuerzo tiene un éxito promedio de 0.005. Alcanza esto sin reejecuciones del modelo base y con un mínimo de llamadas adicionales al modelo.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Para agentes de IA personales que manejan datos sensibles (email, archivos, pagos), SPILLWAY proporciona un nivel auditable de rechazo de acciones, manteniendo la utilidad del agente y la seguridad contra ataques de inyección de prompts, crucial para la confianza y adopción.

papers.title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
papers.abstract_en: Biomolecular foundation models predict the structures of proteins and their complexes accurately, and large language models (LLMs) reason in natural language, but the two remain separate: the abilities of the former are not part of a general-purpose LLM, and the reasoning of the latter does not enter a structure prediction. Calpha aims at one general model that folds proteins and complexes, understands protein sequence and structure, and lets its language reasoning influence the structures it predicts. This report covers the first step, in which an LLM outputs single-chain protein structures. Qwen3.5-9B reads a sequence enriched with ESM2 residue features. It can respond in text or emit a token that invokes a pretrained SimpleFold structure head, which receives information about the protein only through Qwen's residue states. Under a fixed folding request, the head achieves mean TM-scores of 0.808 on the FoldBench-334 development set, 0.635 on CASP16 domains and 0.900 on a CAMEO-style PDB set. We compare these predictions with a baseline in which ESM2-3B encodes the sequence and a fine-tuned SimpleFold-3B head predicts the coordinates. The two systems also differ in trainable weights, training duration and crop length. For chains of 100--299 residues, all three paired confidence intervals include zero. At 300--600 residues, the mean differences are -0.044, -0.160 and -0.025, respectively. In a separate test, four English request types triggered folding on every evaluated example. Protein training reduced accuracy on a 350-item MMLU-Pro subset from 77.4% to 70.3%. An LLM can therefore output single-chain structures from its own states, with lower long-chain scores in the current comparisons and reduced accuracy on the evaluated MMLU-Pro subset. Complex prediction, structure understanding and the effect of language reasoning on the predicted coordinates remain future work.

summary_es.tldr: Calpha integra modelos de lenguaje con predicción de estructuras de proteínas, permitiendo razonamiento biomolecular y lingüístico en un solo modelo.
summary_es.problema: Los modelos de IA para predecir estructuras de proteínas y los modelos de lenguaje grandes (LLMs) operan de forma separada, sin compartir sus capacidades.
summary_es.propuesta: Calpha es un modelo general que integra la predicción de estructuras de proteínas y la comprensión del lenguaje natural, permitiendo que el razonamiento del LLM influya en las estructuras predichas. Este primer paso se enfoca en que un LLM prediga estructuras de cadenas de proteínas únicas.
summary_es.resultados: El modelo logra puntuaciones TM de 0.808 en FoldBench-334, 0.635 en dominios CASP16 y 0.900 en un conjunto estilo CAMEO. Para cadenas de 300-600 residuos, las diferencias medias con un baseline son de -0.044, -0.160 y -0.025. La precisión en un subconjunto MMLU-Pro se redujo del 77.4% al 70.3% tras el entrenamiento con proteínas.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite unificar el razonamiento biomolecular y lingüístico en un solo modelo de IA, abriendo la puerta a avances en el diseño de fármacos, medicina personalizada y comprensión de procesos biológicos.

papers.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
papers.abstract_en: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2x without a separate draft model. Our release follows the LLM360 definition of open source for transparency and reproducibility: the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code, notably our production-scale xLLM framework for dense and MoE training and the RL360 reinforcement-learning stack. Beyond the data itself, we release and document in detail every pipeline that built it, the part of model development that open releases most rarely disclose. These pipelines produced roughly 10T synthetic pre-training tokens, showing that synthetic data can be a major ingredient of pre-training at scale. Four of the models share one 22T-token pre-training corpus and recipe, revealing consistent scaling behavior and enabling controlled studies of scale and sparsity. All artifacts are available at https://ifm.ai/k2/

summary_es.tldr: Presentamos K2-Horizon, modelos de lenguaje abiertos y potentes para razonamiento y tareas complejas, con innovaciones en arquitectura y datos.
summary_es.problema: La necesidad de modelos de lenguaje de IA potentes, abiertos y transparentes para tareas complejas de razonamiento, codificación y automatización, con un enfoque en la eficiencia y la reproducibilidad.
summary_es.propuesta: Lanzamiento de K2-Horizon, una flota de seis modelos de lenguaje totalmente abiertos (0.9B a 375B MoE), introduciendo Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA) y softplus attention gating para mejorar el razonamiento, y adaptadores de difusión Uno para acelerar la decodificación. Se libera todo el historial de desarrollo, datos y código.
summary_es.resultados: Los modelos son competitivos con modelos abiertos de su tamaño en benchmarks de agentes y codificación. El modelo 36B-A4B con MoVA y softplus iguala casi a un modelo denso de 32B con 1/7 de parámetros activos. Los adaptadores Uno aceleran la decodificación hasta 2.2x. Se usaron ~10T tokens sintéticos.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Fomenta la investigación y el desarrollo en IA al proporcionar modelos de vanguardia, transparentes y reproducibles, acelerando la adopción de IA en diversas aplicaciones profesionales y de investigación.

papers.title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Sage S1.5 Flash, a 320-billion-parameter general-purpose mixture-of-experts model designed to reason over scientific evidence and act in interactive environments. Sage Sci-Perception uses dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences and represents spectra as ordered patches of measurements. Modality-specific projectors map these representations into the input space of a shared backbone, which processes them alongside text and images. To develop the model's agent capabilities, we construct verifiable environments for tool use, search, and coding, as well as specialized workflows involving machine learning experiments and scientific software. Task completion is checked against execution results, changes in environment state, or submitted artifacts. We evaluate Sage S1.5 Flash on 33 benchmarks across seven domains. In the primary comparison against five baselines, it ranks first on OfficeQA Pro (72.2), MLE-bench Lite (90.3 HumanRank), Harvey LAB, and SpreadsheetBench~2, and second on OSWorld-Verified (85.2), WebArena-Verified (67.6), and DeepResearch Bench~II (54.2). These results show particular strengths in using documentary evidence, producing verifiable workbooks, and carrying out machine learning tasks, alongside competitive performance in desktop and browser workflows that require the model to act on visual feedback.

summary_es.tldr: Sage S1.5 Flash: un modelo de IA de 320B parámetros para razonar sobre ciencia y actuar en entornos interactivos.
summary_es.problema: El paper aborda la necesidad de modelos de IA capaces de procesar información científica multimodal (moléculas, secuencias, espectros) y actuar de forma verificable en entornos complejos como el uso de herramientas, codificación y experimentos de machine learning.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone Sage S1.5 Flash, un modelo de expertos mixtos (MoE) de 320 mil millones de parámetros con codificadores específicos para grafos moleculares, secuencias biológicas y espectros. Se mapean estas modalidades a un backbone compartido con texto e imágenes, y se entrena en entornos verificables para el uso de herramientas, codificación y tareas de ML.
summary_es.resultados: Sage S1.5 Flash obtiene el primer puesto en OfficeQA Pro (72.2), MLE-bench Lite (90.3 HumanRank), Harvey LAB y SpreadsheetBench~2. Queda en segundo lugar en OSWorld-Verified (85.2), WebArena-Verified (67.6) y DeepResearch Bench~II (54.2) frente a cinco bases de comparación.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Demuestra la capacidad de la IA para integrar y razonar sobre datos científicos complejos y realizar tareas prácticas y verificables, abriendo puertas a la automatización en investigación y desarrollo científico.

papers.title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
papers.abstract_en: Advancing medical AI for inclusive healthcare requires evaluation across diverse healthcare roles, tasks, and care settings, but benchmark coverage remains uneven. We introduce InclusionMed, an open medical AI evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare. The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities. For the first release, we selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction. With InclusionMed-DxFiles, our private diagnostic reasoning benchmark, the Atlas contains five benchmarks covering three of its nine role--capability cells. We evaluated frontier large language models on the Atlas and aggregated their results into the InclusionMed Index, with overall scores ranging from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100. The Index also reports scores by healthcare role and AI capability, showing that a model's rank varied with the role or capability considered. A within-benchmark analysis using task-level tags showed that the ten highest-ranked models in the Index all scored higher on patient communication than on clinical decision-making. Models with similar Index scores also differed substantially in estimated inference cost. These findings highlight the need for evaluation covering more diverse healthcare needs and for context-specific model selection. Through open collaboration and community contributions, InclusionMed seeks to ensure that diverse healthcare needs worldwide shape how medical AI progress is defined and measured.

summary_es.tldr: InclusionMed evalúa la IA médica para asegurar que beneficie a todos los profesionales y pacientes en diversos entornos de atención.
summary_es.problema: La evaluación de la IA médica actual es desigual y no cubre la diversidad de roles, tareas y entornos de atención sanitaria, lo que limita la inclusión.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce InclusionMed, una iniciativa abierta para evaluar la IA médica, organizada en un Atlas que cubre roles (médico, enfermero, administrador) y capacidades de IA (diagnóstico, comunicación, toma de decisiones). Incluye benchmarks públicos y uno privado (InclusionMed-DxFiles).
summary_es.resultados: Se evaluaron modelos de lenguaje avanzados, obteniendo puntuaciones en el InclusionMed Index entre 17.5 y 49.1/100. Los modelos destacaron más en comunicación con el paciente que en toma de decisiones clínicas. Los costes de inferencia variaron significativamente entre modelos con puntuaciones similares.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Es crucial para seleccionar modelos de IA médica adecuados al contexto y asegurar que la tecnología beneficie equitativamente a todos los profesionales y pacientes, promoviendo una atención sanitaria más inclusiva y eficiente.

papers.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
papers.abstract_en: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers. This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating. Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator. To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base. Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output. On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.

summary_es.tldr: MovieRoll optimiza la generación de videos largos en streaming, manteniendo calidad y eficiencia con técnicas innovadoras.
summary_es.problema: Generar videos largos en streaming de forma continua y con alta calidad, superando las limitaciones de la ventana de entrenamiento y los costos de caché.
summary_es.propuesta: MovieRoll utiliza un marco de base a destilado que combina afinamiento en streaming, destilación de 'long-rollout' y inferencia de largo alcance. Emplea Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF) para el entrenamiento base, compresión jerárquica de caché KV (HieraKV) para eficiencia, y ajuste acumulativo con destilación de coincidencia de distribución (CuLT-DMD) para el entrenamiento de largo alcance.
summary_es.resultados: MovieRoll-Base mantiene competitividad a 30s. MovieRoll-Distilled logra las puntuaciones más altas en HeliosBench hasta 60s, combinando naturalidad y movimiento activo, con una reducción de caché de hasta 78% gracias a HieraKV.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite la creación eficiente y de alta calidad de contenido de video extenso para plataformas de streaming, mejorando la experiencia del usuario y reduciendo costos computacionales.

papers.title: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
papers.abstract_en: In many long-horizon settings, an agent's own choices create future constraints: committing finite capacity establishes future obligations and forecloses later opportunities. Sustaining performance therefore requires both keeping evolving plans feasible and comparing the value of resource allocations with the alternatives they displace. Recent benchmarks increasingly evaluate LLM agents in continuing operations, but give less attention to how agents keep their own commitments feasible while reassessing resource allocations as opportunities change. We introduce OutfitterBench, where agents manage an outdoor-equipment rental business for 200 days, purchasing from a 46-product catalog and handling roughly 1,100 reservation requests. Under a fixed capital ceiling, reservations and uncertain walk-in demand compete for reusable equipment whose availability changes over time. Experiments with seven frontier LLMs show that several agents underperform a simple rule-based baseline, while only the leading agent consistently surpasses it. Trajectory analysis shows that some agents apply known constraints inconsistently and make new decisions that conflict with existing commitments. Agents with more reliable fulfillment can still secure low returns from comparable commitments or delay resource reallocation. The leading agent better connects preparation with economic choices but also misses opportunities for more profitable asset use. These findings highlight limitations in sustaining coherent resource plans and reassessing their value over time. The benchmark code is publicly available at https://github.com/adminblackjack/OutfitterBench.

summary_es.tldr: Evalúa la capacidad de los agentes LLM para gestionar recursos a largo plazo, coordinando compromisos y asignación de inventario en un negocio de alquiler de equipos.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes LLM actuales tienen dificultades para mantener la viabilidad de sus planes a largo plazo, especialmente al gestionar recursos finitos y coordinar compromisos cambiantes, lo que afecta su rendimiento en operaciones continuas.
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce OutfitterBench, un benchmark que simula la gestión de un negocio de alquiler de equipos durante 200 días, con 46 productos, ~1100 solicitudes y demanda incierta, bajo un capital fijo y recursos reutilizables con disponibilidad variable.
summary_es.resultados: Siete LLMs de vanguardia fueron evaluados; varios agentes tuvieron un rendimiento inferior a una línea base simple basada en reglas. Solo el agente líder superó consistentemente la línea base. El análisis de trayectorias reveló inconsistencias en la aplicación de restricciones y conflictos con compromisos existentes.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Este trabajo identifica limitaciones clave en la capacidad de los agentes LLM para mantener planes de recursos coherentes y reevaluar su valor a lo largo del tiempo, crucial para aplicaciones prácticas en logística, gestión de inventario y planificación a largo plazo.
